Run jobs, each in its own R process

Source: R/process_isolation.R
fb_isolated_lapply.Rd

fb_isolated_lapply() is lapply() with each call of fn made in a separate R process started through callr, so that a process ended by the operating system or by a crash in compiled code is reported as a refusal and the session goes on. It is the mechanism behind options(flexyBayes.isolation = "process"), offered to packages that extend flexyBayes for their own loops of model fits.

Usage

fb_isolated_lapply(jobs, fn, plan = list())

Arguments

jobs

A list or vector, fn is called on each element.

fn

A function of one element of jobs.

plan

A list:

  • workers: how many processes run at once, a whole number of one or more (default 1).

  • threads_per_worker: the OpenMP threads each process may use, or NA (default) to leave them as the session has them. A process also runs one chain at a time when this is set.

  • warm_first: TRUE runs the first job alone before the others start, so that a Stan program compiled by it is cached for the rest (default FALSE).

  • engine: the engine the jobs fit with, named in a refusal (default "none").

  • entry_point: the function the user called, named in a refusal (default "fb_isolated_lapply()").

Value

A list of the values fn returned, in the order of jobs.

Details

Each process loads flexyBayes, and the package whose namespace fn is defined in, from where this session loaded them, and starts from this session's flexyBayes, brms, cmdstanr and INLA settings, its environment variables and its random-number state. Messages, warnings and printed output come back and are replayed in job order, never in completion order. A job that fails stops new jobs from starting. The jobs before it are waited for, and the lowest failing job's error is raised. With one worker, each process starts from the random-number state the previous one left, as lapply() would, with several, each starts from the session's state and the session's state is left where it was.

A process that ends without returning raises the refusal isolated_process_died, which names the engine, the entry point, the job and the signal or exit status.

See also

fb_refit(), the refit that such jobs usually run.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && requireNamespace("callr", quietly = TRUE)
fb_isolated_lapply(1:2, function(i) i^2, list(workers = 2L))
}
